transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-01 11:00 AM PT | Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Olivia (Redwood CSM), Hannah (Cobalt Legal), Ethan (CTO), Priya (Procurement), Marco (DevOps), Taylor (Security)

Auto-summary (auto): Align on DPA redlines and SLA minimums; confirm pilot pricing; schedule bench + technical deep dive.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Hannah (Cobalt Legal): Hi — Hannah here.
[00:10] Ethan (CTO): Ethan, on from infra.
[00:12] Priya (Procurement): Priya — procurement.
[00:14] Marco (DevOps): Marco — will be focused on networking.
[00:16] Taylor (Security): Taylor, security.
[00:18] Liam (Redwood SE): Liam here, I’ll handle the performance items.
[00:20] Maya: Great. Agenda — MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets, pricing for a 3-month pilot, and next steps. If anything else add it now.

[01:10] Hannah: Quick note from legal — we scanned Redwood's standard DPA and had several asks: stronger data residency language, KMS key control clarification, and clarification on log retention. Also a question about subprocessor lists and audit rights.

[01:35] Maya: Totally. We can provide KMS integration options — customer-managed keys via our KMS connector or bring-your-own HSM in Private. The subprocessor list is in the security packet, but we can surface a canonical list and, if needed, an audit window.

[02:02] Taylor: For us, it's important that keys never leave our control and that any logs containing PII are redacted before retention. Is that possible with your hosted product?

[02:25] Maya: With hosted we offer encryption at rest and in transit; for full key control you want Redwood Private — that gives the private control plane and customer-managed KMS integration. Hosted can do envelope keys but RBAC to keys is limited.

[03:10] Ethan: So to confirm, Private gives us the ability to manage KMS and have the control plane in our VPC? And does that add a lot to cost?

[03:25] Liam: Correct — Private = customer VPC + optional on-prem package. Cost is higher since you reserve capacity; we'll give you a pricing sheet that contrasts hosted vs dedicated vs private for the pilot. Wanted to mention there are quantization/throughput tradeoffs we often recommend for inference-heavy queries — can show a profile.

[04:00] Priya: On pricing, procurement wants a clear pilot SOW and a not-to-exceed for the pilot. We need monthly caps and clarity on overage billing.

[04:20] Maya: We'll do a pilot SOW with a committed token/embedding allotment and a burst clause. Overage rate spelled out. We can also add a clause for a one-time discount for pilot conversion.

[05:00] Hannah: Back to the DPA, can you accept a clause for data residency — that data for EU customers stays in EU regions and US in US?

[05:20] Maya: Yes — region pinning is part of our routing policy; we can commit region residency in the DPA for the production rollout, pilot we'll try to pin and we'll note any exceptions.

[06:05] Marco: Networking question — what's the egress pattern if we run Private in our VPC? We need to ensure traffic doesn't route through public subnets and want to meter egress.

[06:25] Liam: With Private we deploy connectors in your VPC; egress is controlled by your routing. We also support peered setups and private endpoints. We'll capture the diagram and firewall ports in the technical deep dive.

[07:30] Taylor: On audit logs — we need an immutable audit trail for admin actions, with retention 1 year. Is that in the standard offering?

[07:50] Olivia (CSM): We surface admin audit logs in Console; retention is configurable. For Private, retention can be forwarded to your SIEM or S3, so that meets the immutable requirement — we'll include retention settings in the security packet.

[08:40] Hannah: Also, we have to check the indemnity and liability caps in the MSA. We typically ask for a higher cap for regulated data. Thoughts?

[09:05] Maya: We can open that conversation — standard MSA has a certain cap, but for enterprise/regulated customers we negotiate upward and can add carve-outs for data handling. We'll flag the MSA for AE/legal escalation.

[10:20] Ethan: On SLA — we're focused on tail latency for short-lived queries; our SLAs need to be expressed as 95th and 99th percentile targets, not just average. Can Redwood commit to p95/p99 SLOs?

[10:45] Liam: We publish latency profiles for models. For p95 we can target e.g., 300–500ms depending on model and sequence length; p99 will be higher. For Dedicated we can give stronger guarantees and an SLA-backed target with credits for breaches. We have automatic fallback policies to keep requests served if a pool is degraded.

[11:40] Priya: Are the SLA credits financial or service credits? Procurement prefers financial credits.

[11:55] Maya: We typically offer service credits, but for enterprise Dedicated/Private we can structure financial remediation in the contract. We'll map that out in the MSA redlines.

[12:40] Hannah: Can you explain the rollback and fallback behavior? If you push a new model that regresses quality, what happens?

[13:00] Liam: We have rollout controls — canaries and automatic fallback to previous pinned model variant if quality metrics drop or latency spikes. For pilot we can keep canary traffic to 1–5% until you sign off. There is also a manual rollback path.

[14:10] Marco: For the benchmark, what do you need from us? Input format, sample size, expected concurrency?

[14:30] Liam: Send two representative prompt sets: one short chat-like (~50 tokens) and one long-form (~1k tokens). We'll run concurrency levels of 50, 200, and 500 qps depending on your target. Please include sample rate, auth tokens (temporary), and a brief throughput target. We'll return latency distributions and KV cache hit ratios.

[15:20] Marco: Ok I'll drop those into the shared folder after the call.

[15:35] Priya: Timeline — procurement wants legal signoff and PO within 6 weeks. Is that realistic?

[15:50] Maya: Yes, if DPA redlines are returned quickly and we move to pilot SOW, 4–6 weeks is doable. We'll treat MSA/DPA as priority.

[16:40] Hannah: A few specific DPA asks: 1) Deletion windows 2) Subprocessor notification 3) Right to audit with a third-party auditor — can you accept a scoped audit?

[17:05] Olivia: We accept scoped audits; typically we provide SOC2 reports and can arrange an on-site or third-party audit with notice. Deletion windows and subprocessor notifications are configurable — we'll propose wording.

[18:00] Taylor: Encryption in transit — do you support TLS 1.3 only? We require modern ciphers.

[18:15] Liam: We use TLS 1.2/1.3 on endpoints, our recommended config is TLS1.3, and we can enforce cipher suites for private endpoints.

[19:10] Priya: Any special procurement hurdles on your side? We need contract countersigned and a net-30 PO.

[19:25] Maya: Net-30 is fine for standard pilots; we'll reflect payment terms in the SOW. If you need escrow or different payment terms we'll flag to finance.

[20:10] Hannah: One more — data egress fees. Our finance requires a clear egress model if data leaves region.

[20:25] Maya: We'll include egress costing in the pricing sheet and show per-GB rates for cross-region egress. For Private we can avoid cross-region egress since data stays in your VPC.

[21:05] Ethan: Competitors also pitched lower headline costs, but with higher latency. We care more about predictable tail latency and auditability.

[21:30] Maya: Totally get it. Our position is predictable economics + observability. Redwood Console will show per-route token cost, latency histograms, and trace links.

[22:40] Hannah: For DPA redlines I'll consolidate and indicate must-haves vs negotiables.

[23:00] Maya: Great. On the SOW: we'll propose a 3-month pilot with a committed token cap, one model variant, and two private vs hosted pricing lines so you can choose. We'll include a clause to convert pilot committed usage toward production reserved capacity if you sign within 30 days.

[24:10] Marco: For the technical deep-dive, I'd like to see the networking diagram, firewall ports, and an IAM map.

[24:25] Liam: We'll prepare a deep-dive pack and do a runbook walkthrough. That will include the KV cache behaviour and recommended batching settings per workload.

[25:40] Taylor: Security packet please — SOC2, pen test summary, subprocessor list, KMS architecture.

[25:55] Olivia: We'll attach the security packet and the SOC2 link in the follow-up email.

[26:30] Hannah: Regarding liability caps — we need suggested alternative language for regulated data protection. Can you prepare that for legal review?

[26:50] Maya: Yes we'll escalate to our legal ops and include proposed language.

[28:00] Priya: Small ask — can you include sample invoice and PO flow so our finance can pre-approve?

[28:15] Maya: Yes, will include invoice template and PO instructions in the follow-up.

[30:05] Liam: Quick technical note — if you plan to hit high concurrency with long sequences, the recommendation is to enable prefix caching and a mid-quantization profile; that reduces cost and improves p99. We'll test both in the bench.

[31:00] Marco: Sounds good.

[32:15] Hannah: Any reference customers for private deployment in finance?

[32:30] Maya: We have a couple of finance logos using Dedicated/Private — I'll include anonymized case studies and a short readout on latency and compliance controls.

[34:00] Ethan: Onboarding timeline — if we get redlines back by 5/6 and pricing by 5/4, we should be able to approve pilot PO by 5/20. That's compressed but doable.

[35:10] Priya: We'll target 5/20 as the sign date.

[35:45] Maya: Ok last check — any blockers?

[36:00] Taylor: For security, we need to review pen test summary and confirm no PII in logs by default; otherwise blocked.

[36:20] Olivia: We'll provide logging controls and log redaction options.

[37:40] Maya: Perfect. I'll summarize and send a follow-up with the SOW, pricing sheet, security packet, and request for DPA redlines.

[38:10] Hannah: We'll do redlines and get back.

[38:25] Marco: I'll upload sample prompts and infra details to the shared folder today.

[39:00] Liam: Thanks — I’ll schedule the benchmark and note the concurrency targets.

[40:15] Maya: Anything else?

[40:25] Priya: Nope.

[40:30] Maya: Ok thanks everyone. Recap of action items and owners will be in the follow-up.

[41:00] Hannah: Thanks.
[41:10] Ethan: Thanks all.
[41:20] Maya: Bye.

(End of recording)
